prompt:
Solve the running-time recurrence below.

```formula essential
T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n
where
T: the running time on input size n
n: the input size
In words: Four half-size calls are followed by linear outside work.
```

Assume bounded positive base-case costs and the usual integer rounding of fractional child sizes.

options.explanation: This is the two-child merge-sort recurrence. Four children instead give a quadratic leaf count.
This assumes matching root and leaf growth. Here linear outside work is polynomially smaller than quadratic leaves, so no extra logarithm is added.
Root domination requires outside work polynomially larger than leaf growth. The stated outside work is smaller instead.
Correct. Four half-size calls give critical exponent two, while linear outside work is smaller by a full power. Leaves dominate.

workedExample: Four children each halve the size. With linear outside work, their combined level cost doubles each generation. The growing geometric series is dominated by the quadratic number of constant-cost leaves. The total is Θ(n²), without an extra logarithm, for original input size n.

link.title: MIT: Master theorem and its conditions

prompt: Toom-3 splits long integers into three parts and replaces nine part-products with five roughly third-size recursive products, plus linear outside work. What explains the improved growth over using all nine?

options.text: Splitting into thirds alone guarantees linear time
options.explanation: The number of recursive children matters as well as their size.

options.text: The linear outside work becomes zero
options.explanation: Interpolation and combination still require work.

options.text: Every recursive call is constant time
options.explanation: Only bounded-size base cases have constant cost.

options.text: Fewer children reduce the leaf-growth exponent while outside work stays below it
options.explanation: Correct. Five instead of nine third-size products create a smaller leaf-dominated recursion tree.

workedExample: Hold the shrink factor fixed and reduce branching. Each generation now creates fewer descendants, reducing the exponent that governs leaf count. Linear outside work remains polynomially below that leaf growth. The exact exponent can be looked up; the mechanism is avoiding recursive products.
